drivingQuestion: Does the mishna's 'one' siman in a bird mean either the gullet or the windpipe, or specifically the gullet?
outcomeNote: The dispute is stated and each side's reading of the mishna given; it is tested and decided only in the following unit (chullin.sugya067).

segments.he: אֶחָד בָּעוֹף אִיתְּמַר: רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר: אוֹ וֶושֶׁט אוֹ קָנֶה, רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה אָמַר: וֶושֶׁט וְלֹא קָנֶה. רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר: אוֹ וֶושֶׁט אוֹ קָנֶה – ״אֶחָד״ קָתָנֵי, ״אֶחָד״ כֹּל דְּהוּ. רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה אָמַר: וֶושֶׁט וְלֹא קָנֶה – מַאי ״אֶחָד״? מְיוּחָד.
segments.en: § The mishna teaches that in the case of one who cuts «one» siman «in a bird,» his slaughter is valid. «It was stated» that there is an amoraic dispute with regard to this matter. «Rav Naḥman said:» One may cut «either the gullet or the windpipe. Rav Adda bar Ahava said:» One must cut the «gullet» for the slaughter to be valid, «but» cutting «the windpipe» is «not» sufficient. The Gemara explains the formulation of the mishna according to the opinion of each amora. «Rav Naḥman said:» One may cut «either the gullet or the windpipe. One» siman «is taught» in the mishna, meaning that the slaughter is valid if he severs «one,» indicating that «either» siman is valid. «Rav Adda bar Ahava said:» One must cut the «gullet» for the slaughter to be valid, «but» cutting «the windpipe» is «not» sufficient. «What» is the meaning of: «One,» in the mishna? It means the «special» one, the gullet.
